source.publication: 2025 Form 80-100 Resident, Non-Resident and Part-Year Resident Individual Income Tax Instructions (Rev. 12/25) and the 2025 Form 80-105 Resident Return (Rev. 09/25); Miss. Admin. Code Title 35 Part III Income and Franchise (Department of Revenue income tax regulations)
source.section: Form 80-105 page 1 lines 8-17 and page 2 lines 38-66; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status and Exemptions table; p.6 Additional Exemptions, Lines 8-12; p.7 Lines 14-17; p.22 Tax Rates; p.27 Schedule of Tax Computation lines 1-4; Instructions PDF p.11 Line 46 Total Pensions and Annuities; FAQ 'Is retirement income taxable?'; Instructions PDF p.5 Filing Status for Married Persons; Miss. Admin. Code Title 35 Part III Subpart 02 Chapter 07 rules 100, 102 and 105 (https://www.sos.ms.gov/adminsearch/ACCode/00000158c.pdf, PDF p.18)

worked: Federal AGI = employer plan distribution (person 0) 40,000.00 + private pension (person 1) 30,000.00 + wages (person 1) 30,000.00 = 100,000.00. Federal taxable income = 100,000.00 - 31,500.00 federal standard deduction = 68,500.00 (given, not tested; the federal senior deduction is ignored). Form 80-105 filing status box 1, Married - Combined or Joint Return. Start at federal AGI 100,000.00 (Mississippi builds its own income on lines 38 to 66; the projection starts from federal AGI and takes out the exempt income, the same result here). Less retirement income, each person on their own: person 0's 401(k) payout 40,000.00 (regulation rule 102: a deferred compensation payout counts once the recipient qualifies for other retirement income by minimum age, years of service or other criteria; person 0, 63, is taken to have met the plan's test; rule 100 exempts it) and person 1's private pension 30,000.00 (rule 100; Line 46 exempt in total; recipient taken to have met the plan requirements); together 70,000.00. Line 66 and line 13 Mississippi AGI = 30,000.00 (person 1's wages; Column A, person 0, has no taxable income). Line 14 standard deduction 4,600.00. Line 8 age boxes checked 0; line 10 = 0 x 1,500.00 = 0.00; line 11 12,000.00; line 12 and line 15 = 12,000.00. Line 16 Mississippi taxable income = 30,000.00 - 4,600.00 - 12,000.00 = 13,400.00. Schedule of Tax Computation line 1: first 10,000.00 x 0% = 0.00; line 2: remaining 3,400.00 x 4.4% = 149.60; line 4 and line 17 = 149.60. Lines 18 and 19 credits 0.00; line 20 = 149.60. The form rounds to whole dollars (p.22), which would give 150; expected keeps the formula result. Only one spouse has income Mississippi taxes, so there is one 10,000 band on the return and projection and form agree.
accepted_approximations: Mississippi builds its own income (Form 80-105 lines 38 to 66); the projection starts from federal AGI and removes the exempt income through the reliefs and Social Security treatment.

IRA, 401(k), 403(b) and 457 payouts and Roth conversions are exempted at every age. Mississippi exempts them only when they are not early distributions (regulation rule 104), and a deferred compensation payout only once the person qualifies for other retirement income by minimum age, years of service or other criteria (rule 102). A projection cannot test either, so an early payout is exempted here; the warning names it for anyone under 60.
